datasets.name: 3d_earthmodel_Lloyd_et_al_2024_GJI
datasets.source: Lloyd, A. J., et al. 'GIA imaging of 3-D mantle viscosity based on palaeo sea level observations - Part I: Sensitivity kernels for an Earth with laterally varying viscosity.' Geophysical Journal International 236.2 (2024): 1139-1171.
datasets.description: Global 3D mantle viscosity (log10 Pa s) inferred from the shear-wave speeds of GLAD-M25, not inverted from GIA data. This is the unmodified initial inference (Fig. S2 of the paper), not the filtered and bounded model of the paper's GIA simulations. Above 400 km it uses the calibration of Richards et al. (2020), below 400 km the approach of Austermann et al. (2021). The authors set the volume average of log10 viscosity to about log10(5e20) from the base of the lithosphere to 670 km and about log10(5e21) below; the crust is a constant 1.5e26 Pa s. Values above 1e30 Pa s, in cratonic lithosphere down to 195 km and beneath Central America at 2750-2800 km, are kept as published. Resampled to the 65,341-point layers of the seismic models (about 88 km spacing), coarser than the 0.5 degree source.
datasets.author: Lloyd, A. J., Crawford, O., Al-Attar, D., Austermann, J., Hoggard, M. J., Richards, F. D., & Syvret, F.
